newsitem.title: USA: House approves breast cancer research stamp.
newsitem.headline: House approves breast cancer research stamp.

text.p: The House voted 422-3 late Tuesday to approve a measure creating a breast cancer postage stamp to help fund research into the disease.
The stamp would be priced one cent above the normal first-class postage, with the extra penny earmarked for breast cancer research. At current rates, the special stamp would cost 33 cents.
The Post Office had opposed creating a stamp to raise money for one specific cause, but lawmakers argued that it made sense to raise money for research on the deadly disease.
The Senate approved similar legislation last week.

The House bill would funnel 70 percent of the revenues generated by sale of the new stamp to fund National Institutes of Health research on breast cancer, with 30 percent going to Defence Department studies.
